metadata.title: The Best Options Trading Platforms for Investors

content.text:
When you buy through links on our articles, Future and its syndication partners may earn a commission.
It's not an easy task to identify the best options trading platforms among an expanding number of choices. Getting your selection right is vital: The tools your platform provides can help you maximize and also protect your portfolio's value.
So the time you take here for high-level look at five of the best options trading platforms, including distinct features and potential drawbacks, is well spent.
We'll examine pros and cons so you can identify the one most suitable for your objectives and see what call options and put options can do for you and your portfolio.
Here are five of the best options trading platforms for investors.
Robinhood
Pros:
-
Comprehensive investment options: Robinhood is low-cost, app-based service, but it supports an array of investment choices. You can manage your portfolio with a single account, and you'll have ample opportunity for diversification.
-
User-friendly interface: The platform is geared toward beginners with relatively small accounts, with zero account minimums and zero-commission trading for stock and ETF options. At the same time, its smart layout makes it useful for investors and traders of all experience levels.
-
Educational resources: Robinhood has developed solid educational resources about options and other investing topics with beginners in mind.
Cons:
-
Improving analytical tools: Robinhood has actually upgraded its tools for profit-and-loss modeling and detailing complex, multi-leg strategies, as well as advanced charting with its Robinhood Legend upgrade.
-
Payment for order flow: Robinhood relies on payment for order flow (PFOF), which can lead to wider bid-ask spreads and less favorable executions for options trades.
InteractiveBrokers
Pros:
-
Versatility and global market access: InteractiveBrokers caters to experienced investors with diverse needs, offering advanced analytical tools and access to global markets.
-
Robust research: The platform provides access to in-depth market research and analysis, enabling you to make informed investment decisions.
-
Professional-grade platform: InteractiveBrokers' Trader Workstation is ideal for seasoned investors seeking advanced features and tools, including multi-leg order capabilities.
Cons:
-
Strict onboarding requirements: Relative to other platforms, InteractiveBrokers is just harder to access. You must disclose your financial standing, your investment objectives and your years of experience to qualify for an account.
-
Learning curve: The platform's extensive features might require a learning curve, especially for investors new to the world of options trading.
